The theory of relativity is a fundamental theory in physics that describes how space and time are related. It was developed by Albert Einstein in the early 20th century and has since become one of the most important and widely accepted theories in the field of physics.

The theory of relativity consists of two parts: special relativity and general relativity. Special relativity deals with objects moving at constant speeds, while general relativity deals with objects moving at constant speeds and the effects of gravity.
